name: Find In Generic tree
html:
Welcome Back Reader!

We hope that you are finding data structure, Generic trees easy to learn. In this article we will look at the next function of a Generic Tree. Yes, as the title says, Find in generic tree.

If you have successfully understood the previous traversal then this one is going to be an easy problem for you. You can first give this problem a try. Before you become restless for How and Why, let's get started with the problem.

Important Links : Problem Link, Question Video

Problem Discussion :

In this problem you are given a partially written GenericTree class. All you need to do is to complete the body of the find function.

The function is expected to find the given data in the tree, if that data is present in the tree then it should return true otherwise return false. Input and Output is managed for you.

You can also check the question video for better understanding of the question.

Watch video Approach :
  • The problem here is to find a particular node in the given input generic tree.
  • The problem is relatively simple and based on traversals on the tree.
  • Here we only need to traverse the tree and check for every node whether the current node is the desired node or not.
  • We do this using recursion by defining Expectation and Faith.
  • Our Expectation from the function find() will be that it returns true if anywhere in the tree function finds the given data otherwise it returns false.
  • And faith is that all the children of the root node already know how to perform this task. All the children will be asked whether their sub tree has the data as an element at any position.
  • If yes, then we return true and if we reach the end of the branch then we return false, if in any case, we get true then we can simply return true without checking the rest of the children.

Consider the following example:

  • Suppose we need to check for the node with value 110,
  • Firstly we are at the root node i.e., the node with value 10 which is not equal to 110 (10 != 110).
  • Traversing to its first child we reach, the node with value 20 which is also not equal to 110 (20 != 110)
  • Then we reach node with value 50 which is also not equal to 110 (50 !=110)
  • We reach children of 50 which are null hence return false.
  • We reach node with value 60 which is also not equal to 110 (60!=110)
  • We reach children of 60 which are null hence return false.
  • Now we reach the second child of the root node i.e., the node with value 30 which is also not equal to 110 (30 != 110)
  • We reach node with value 70 which is also not equal to 110 (70!=110)
  • We reach children of 70 which are null hence return false.
  • Now we reach second child of node 30 i.e. node 80 which is also not equal to 110 (80 != 110)
  • We reach node with value 110 which is equal to 110 (110 ==110)
  • Hence we return true.
  • Now we reach the calls of the root node and we return true as our result.

Let's try to code this

  1. First of all we check the data of the node at which we are standing.
  2. If the data matches the data of the node then we return true from here only. No further statement will run in such a case.
  3. A for loop is applied to access all the children of Node node one by one.
  4. Inside this for loop, we make a recursive call to each child until we find the data and store this result in variable fic (find in child).
  5. We check if this variable is true. It means that data was present in the child branch to which the last call was made.
  6. So we return true because there is no need to make further calls. As we have found the data.
  7. If fic were false then control comes out of the for loop and we return false.
Pseudo Code

You have already done the linearize a generic tree problem. So, the approach is going to be similar. We are going to use recursion to solve this problem.

  1. High level Thinking: In the high level thinking we have established a faith that if we call the function linearize(node) for the children of the root node then they will be linearized and will return their tail respectively.
  2. Joining the tail: Since the tail gets returned to us, we will remove the last child node and in the tail of the second last child node, we will add the last child node as its child.
  3. Low-Level Thinking: On applying the low-level thinking, we can understand the base case of the recursion. We have to return whenever we get a leaf node as it has no children. The tail of a leaf node is itself the leaf node itself and we cannot linearize it.
import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public class Main { private static class Node { int data; ArrayList< Node> children = new ArrayList< >(); } public static void display(Node node) { String str = node.data + " -> "; for (Node child : node.children) { str += child.data + ", "; } str += "."; System.out.println(str); for (Node child : node.children) { display(child); } } public static Node construct(int[] arr) { Node root = null; Stack< Node> st = new Stack< >(); for (int i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) { if (arr[i] == -1) { st.pop(); } else { Node t = new Node(); t.data = arr[i]; if (st.size() > 0) { st.peek().children.add(t); } else { root = t; } st.push(t); } } return root; } public static boolean find(Node node, int data) { if (node.data == data) { return true; } for (Node child : node.children) { boolean fic = find(child, data); if (fic) { return true; } } return false; } public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(br.readLine()); int[] arr = new int[n]; String[] values = br.readLine().split(" "); for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { arr[i] = Integer.parseInt(values[i]); } int data = Integer.parseInt(br.readLine()); Node root = construct(arr); boolean flag = find(root, data); System.out.println(flag); // display(root); } }
java; true"; Analysis: Time Complexity:

O(n)

We travel to all the elements of the tree. Every node is processed individually in a while loop.

Space Complexity:

O(1)

No extra space is used. But when the function runs at that time, space acquired by the memory stack will be O(n).
